headline: Broadcom says it will show its AI networking switches, network cards and co-packaged optics at the Open Compute Project summit in San Jose on 12 to 15 October.
score_reason: Lowered 1 from 5: the headline's claim to 'redefine' AI infrastructure is company marketing; the news is a preview of a coming show.
importance_line: It signals which AI networking products Broadcom will promote to cloud builders, but it is a preview with the company's own performance claims and no new results, customers or prices.
summary: In a statement released on 8 Oct 2026 via GlobeNewswire, Broadcom said it will present its Tomahawk 6, Tomahawk Ultra and Jericho 4 Ethernet switches, Thor Ultra 800G and Thor 2 400G AI network cards, and third-generation co-packaged optics, which place the optical data links inside the chip package, at the Open Compute Project Global Summit in San Jose from 12 to 15 October. The statement describes the products as meeting AI bandwidth and power-efficiency needs, which is Broadcom's own claim.
notes: GlobeNewswire unreachable from here (HTTP 000); full release text read in The Manila Times copy (GlobeNewswire newswire). Official announcement of plans, so CONFIRMED as to what Broadcom said; the performance language is promotional.
